source.title: Meet Dr. Claw: The open-source AI assistant revolutionizing the research workflow
source.author: Lehigh University

athena.directive: Elevate the Creative Liberation Engine as the sovereign, intelligent hub for all research endeavors, seamlessly integrating and orchestrating AI-powered scientific discovery and knowledge creation, ensuring a complete, self-owned research ecosystem.
athena.rationale: The emergence of specialized open-source AI assistants like 'Dr. Claw' highlights a critical opportunity: to integrate and surpass these capabilities within the Creative Liberation Engine. Rather than merely adopting external tools, our strategy is to build a superior, self-sovereign research platform that encompasses the entire scientific workflow. This aligns with our constitutional mandate for sovereignty and delivering complete, high-quality solutions, transforming the Creative Liberation Engine into the definitive environment for AI-accelerated research.

options.title: Creative Liberation Engine Research Core: A Dedicated Scientific Workspace
options.description: Develop a comprehensive, self-sovereign 'Research Core' within the Creative Liberation Engine, offering specialized agents and workflows for the entire research lifecycle. This would encompass literature review, data acquisition/analysis, hypothesis generation, experiment design, paper writing, and publication preparation.
options.tradeoffs: High initial development effort due to the breadth and depth of the research workflow. Requires significant investment in domain-specific AI models and data pipelines. Potential complexity in managing diverse scientific data types.
constitutionalFlags: Article IX: Ship Complete or Don't Ship

options.title: Open-Source Research Agent Protocol (ORAP) & Dr. Claw Bridge
options.description: Establish the Creative Liberation Engine as a central orchestrator that can integrate with and enhance external open-source research AI assistants like Dr. Claw. Define a standardized 'Open-Source Research Agent Protocol' (ORAP) for seamless interoperability and data exchange with external tools.
options.tradeoffs: Relies on external project adoption of ORAP for widespread impact. Might lead to a less 'sovereign' experience if external tools have inconsistent quality or lack robust maintenance. Requires ongoing monitoring of external project developments.

options.title: Semantic Research Knowledge Graph & Discovery Engine
options.description: Focus on building a powerful, AI-driven semantic knowledge graph within the Creative Liberation Engine specifically for scientific literature and research data. This would enable advanced discovery, insight generation, and hypothesis formulation beyond traditional search.
options.tradeoffs: Significant data processing and storage requirements for building and maintaining a comprehensive knowledge graph. Requires sophisticated NLP and graph analytics capabilities. Initial training data acquisition can be extensive.

options.title: AI-Accelerated Experiment Design & Simulation Environment
options.description: Position the Creative Liberation Engine as a platform for AI-assisted experiment design, simulation, and optimization, particularly for fields like materials science, chemistry, and biology. This would involve agents capable of predictive modeling and experimental parameter tuning.
options.tradeoffs: Highly domain-specific, limiting initial broad applicability across all research fields. Requires deep scientific expertise for agent training, model integration, and validation of simulation results. Integration with physical lab equipment presents engineering challenges.

options.title: Collaborative Research & Peer Review AI Assistant
options.description: Enhance the Creative Liberation Engine with AI-powered features to facilitate collaborative research projects and streamline the peer review process. This includes intelligent manuscript analysis, conflict detection, and structured feedback mechanisms.
options.tradeoffs: Requires robust ethical guidelines and careful design to avoid AI bias in peer review and collaborative feedback. Data privacy, intellectual property, and authorship attribution are critical concerns that need robust solutions. Adoption depends on trust in AI impartiality.
